note: One small idea today: make failed Claude Code runs explain themselves, and stop a timed-out run from leaving stray programs running on your PC. Nothing in the daily sweep needs action; I checked that the new 'retry watchdog' setting would hurt us, so I say no to it.

questions: When a worker's Claude Code run fails (workers.run), do we know why, and does a timeout leave anything running on Windows?
Do the new retry settings (watchdog, 529 delay, fallback model) fit our fail-fast design?
Do the model fallbacks in Claude Code change which model really answers us?
gaps: Searches (13) are under the 15 the job asks for; GitHub queries for headless wrappers and cost tools returned nothing new.
No hq.db in this checkout, so I could not count how often fallback_api or timeouts happen. The idea starts with measuring that.
The docs do not say whether --fallback-model applies to claude -p.

ideas.title: Make failed Claude Code runs explain themselves, and clean up after a timeout
ideas.problem: workers.run turns every failure into Unavailable with a 300-character message, and the only record of a good or bad run is the model_call event with turns/secs. The result's subtype (error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution...) is not logged, so we cannot tell a plan limit from an overloaded API from a hang. Also: on timeout, subprocess.run (workers.py line ~104, atlas_engine._run) kills only the claude process. Claude Code's own docs and an open issue (76353, Windows, still seen on 2.1.272) say child processes of the Bash tool survive a kill. Atlas has Bash(python hq.py), Ghassan has python -m py_compile, so a stuck run can leave a python process behind. Last, the usage row records the configured model, but Claude Code can switch to a fallback model; the real one is only in modelUsage.
ideas.proposal: 1) In workers.run, when not ok, add subtype, terminal error text (first 200 chars) and the keys of modelUsage to a new 'run_failed' event (cp.log) next to the existing model_call; also log the real model(s) from modelUsage in the model_call info and in cp.record_usage. 2) Replace subprocess.run with subprocess.Popen + communicate(timeout); on TimeoutExpired call 'taskkill /F /T /PID <pid>' on Windows (os.killpg with start_new_session on Mac/Linux), then communicate() to collect output. Same change in atlas_engine._run. Put the helper in workers.py (shared). 3) Do NOT enable CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG: it waits out a usage limit for hours, while our design fails fast and parks (LIMIT_UNTIL, cloud Atlas). workers.py and atlas_engine.py are protected from Ghassan, so the Builder chat must make the change.
ideas.gain: Small but real: every fallback_api and every 'Claude Code took too long' gets a cause, so the next reliability idea can be based on counts instead of guesses. No stray python/find processes after a timeout. Measure: after two weeks, group run_failed by subtype and see which cause is biggest; check Task Manager for leftover python.exe after a forced timeout (set WORKER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS low in practice mode).
ideas.test: 1) Normal: a successful run still returns the same output and model_call now lists the real model. 2) Edge: run with --max-turns 1 on a two-step task; the event shows subtype error_max_turns and the message is unchanged for the user. 3) Failure: a fake claude script (practice mode) that spawns a child 'sleep 600' and hangs; after the timeout both processes are gone and Unavailable is raised within 5 seconds of the limit.
ideas.confidence_why: Retry and fallback facts are from official docs (A). The orphan-process leak rests on an open GitHub issue (B) and I have not seen it happen on this PC; how often our runs fail is unmeasured (no hq.db here).
ideas.risks: taskkill /T can kill more than intended if the pid is reused after the process ended: only call it inside the TimeoutExpired branch. Extra logging adds a few events per day. No outside code is adopted.
